title: Bidirectional A*: Catch the Route Faster!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from both start and goal across a real street-grid graph of Valencia. The visualization shows how two coordinated A* frontiers meet to find an efficient shortest path.
ig_caption:
🧭🚦 Valencia’s street map becomes a weighted graph—intersections are nodes, roads are edges. With **Bidirectional A***, we run two informed searches at once: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal, each using a heuristic to guide expansion. 🤝✨

📐 In graph-theory terms: we’re solving the shortest path problem on a road network by maintaining two priority frontiers (best-first by f(n)=g(n)+h(n)) until they meet at an optimal or near-optimal meeting point. Because exploration happens from *both ends*, the visited area shrinks dramatically compared to single-direction A*—especially on large, sparse urban graphs like El Cabanyal’s street layout. 📍🧠

🎥 Want a version overlaying traffic-like weights (time, distance, or turn penalties)? Drop a comment with your preferred start + destination neighborhood! 👇❤️
fb_caption:
Imagine Valencia’s streets as a graph: intersections are nodes, road segments are edges, and each edge can carry a weight like travel time. **Bidirectional A*** searches from both the start and the goal using heuristic guidance, and once the two frontiers meet, it reconstructs an efficient route—showing how informed graph search can cut work dramatically. ✅

If you like algorithm visualizations, share this post with a friend learning pathfinding and comment what city you want next!
yt_description:
Bidirectional A* Pathfinding on Real Street Maps! 🗺️🚦 In this video, we visualize **Bidirectional A*** by running two heuristic-guided searches from start and goal simultaneously. This reduces explored nodes versus classic A*, speeding up shortest-path discovery on weighted graph representations of real city streets (nodes/intersections + edges/road segments).
